# driftd

<!-- badges: start -->
<!-- badges: end -->

driftd provides a streamlined workflow for fitting Drift‑Diffusion Models (DDMs) to trial‑level RT and binary response data, performing participant‑level maximum‑likelihood fits (via `nlminb`/`rtdists`) with standard errors, and checks of model fit that compare observed and predicted response probabilities and RT quantiles.

## Installation

From CRAN (when available):

```r
install.packages("driftd")
```

Development version from GitHub:

```r
devtools::install_github("JStrueder/driftd")
```

## Quick Example: Fitting a DDM and Checking Model Fit

This example demonstrates the typical workflow. Fitting can be slow, so the fitting step is shown with `eval = FALSE`. Use the included example dataset to follow along.

```{r example, eval = FALSE}
library(driftd)

# load example data included with the package
data(example_data)

# Quick inspect
head(example_data)

# Fit the model (this may take time; run interactively)
results <- driftd(
  data = example_data,
  sub_id = "ID",
  response = "R",
  rt = "RT",
  vary_z = c("val"),
  vary_v = c("prob", "val"),
  fix_st0 = TRUE,
  fix_sz = TRUE,
  fix_sv = TRUE,
  print_starting_vals = FALSE
)

# Examine results
results$individual_estimates
results$standard_errors   # asymptotic standard errors (see ?driftd)
results$summary

# Model fit: observed vs predicted response probabilities and RT quantiles,
# with prediction intervals from 200 simulated datasets
pred <- predict(results, seed = 1)

aggregate(pred)        # group averages per condition cell
summary(pred)          # misfit per participant, worst first

plot(pred)                                   # quantile-probability plot
plot(pred, facet = "val")                    # ... split by a condition column
plot(pred, type = "scatter")                 # observed vs predicted, per statistic
plot(pred, type = "cdf")                     # RT distributions per condition cell
plot(pred, type = "participants")            # participants with poor fit
plot(pred, participant = 3)                  # a single participant

# Simulate replicate datasets from the fitted model
sims <- simulate(results, nsim = 10, seed = 1)
```
